note: Every network source this recipe touches, with the digest verified at fetch time. No credentials appear anywhere in this file or in the built image.

base_image.note: Same pinned digest already verified by latex/benchmark/candidates/tinytex-v86. Docker's linux/386 platform on an amd64 host needs no binfmt/QEMU emulation: the host CPU executes 32-bit x86 instructions natively, only the userland ABI (dpkg arch i386) differs. Confirmed with `docker run --rm --platform=linux/386 debian:bookworm-slim dpkg --print-architecture` -> i386.

requirement_evidence.conclusion: bcf format 3.11 requires Biber 2.21, matching manifest.releases.<id>.bibliography.biber.compatible = ["2.21"] in docs/specs/wasmtex-interfaces.md section 1.
requirement_evidence.local_texlive_2025_cross_check: The developer machine's TeX Live 2025 (nixos.org build) also ships biblatex with \blx@bcfversion{3.11}, so the local fixture .bcf used for vm-smoke.mjs is bit-compatible with the browser release's expectation.

a_debian_bookworm_package.detail: `apt-cache policy biber` inside the i386 bookworm-slim container reports candidate 2.18-1, older than the required 2.21.

b_texlive_i386_linux_binary.detail: TeX Live 2026's dated historic snapshot repository (https://texlive.info/historic/systems/texlive/2026/tlnet-final/) returns 404 as of this build (2026 has not been archived as a historic/final year yet). The current rolling mirror (https://mirror.ctan.org/systems/texlive/tlnet/) still ships an i386-linux biber binary but its texlive.tlpdb gives no exact upstream version number and would not be reproducible (it moves). TeX Live 2025's frozen tlnet-final repository -- the same one latex/benchmark/candidates/tinytex-v86 already pins and validated -- ships biber.i386-linux revision 75738, and `biber --version` from that archive reports exactly 2.21. Used this: pinned, historic, already-verified elsewhere in this repository.

c_cpan.detail: Option (b) succeeded, so CPAN/Perl compilation (slowest, largest guest) was not attempted.

download.note: The build extracts bin/i386-linux/biber from this archive on the HOST (bookworm-slim ships no xz-utils, and installing one merely to unpack once would add unnecessary guest-image bloat) and COPYs the plain 32-bit ELF executable into the image.
download.runtime_dependencies: ldd inside an i386 bookworm-slim container: linux-gate.so.1 (vDSO), libpthread.so.0, libc.so.6, /lib/ld-linux.so.2 -- all already present in debian:bookworm-slim. No Perl, no fontconfig, no CA certificates, no additional libraries were installed.

v86_runtime.note: Same pinned revision string as latex/benchmark/candidates/tinytex-v86/assets-lock.json for the emulator/runtime files, though this guest carries no TinyTeX packages. See that directory's assets-lock.json for the exact per-file URLs/digests reused here (libv86.js, v86.wasm, seabios.bin, vgabios.bin, buildroot-bzimage68.bin).
v86_runtime.licence_evidence: libv86.js top-of-file header and https://github.com/copy/v86/blob/master/LICENSE both state BSD-2-Clause.

licences.debian_base_image: various OSI licences per Debian package (no packages beyond the base bookworm-slim rootfs are installed in the guest)
